correctness.rationale: The exact boundary-resolvent equation follows from the stated PDE and Robin condition. With positive polar-to-boundary and boundary-to-polar coefficients, weighting the scalar orientation component by f/b makes the full slab generator self-adjoint with a closed semibounded form. Its real spectrum cannot cross through Hopf. The positive Stieltjes resolvent gives the exact positive-eigenvalue criterion. Differentiation reduces global minimization to strictly increasing B_U(y), whose endpoint limits are 0 and infinity; Taylor expansion proves the small-Dr rates. A separate numerical program passed 220 finite checks, supplementing rather than proving the uniform theorems.

value.rationale: Finite solute relaxation is an experimentally and mathematically motivated omission from the source’s quasistatic stability analysis. The result shows rigorously that this memory alone cannot induce oscillatory onset in the isolated polar chemical channel, classifies its entire finite-wave unstable band, and computes a singular quarter-power selected length as rotational diffusion vanishes. It is not merely a different parameter sample, despite its explicit zero-drift and linear scope. The earlier 2015 dynamic-chemical literature limits novelty claims to the exact slab and positive-feedback sector, not to chemical delay or generic polar patterns.
